decisions.rationale: Verified true, so it cannot be rejected. intake.md 'Lab plan' gives the S32 lab three topics. module.json sourceCoverageNotes say 'covering the three S32 topics'. The three S33 topic.json files record lab 'course:react' pointing to course-project parts P3-P5. lab.json covers all six topics, and its note scopes the allowance to 'the module's S32 guided lab slot'. Tasks 4-6 and 8 therefore apply S33 topics one day before S33 teaches them. The catalog lab-field mismatch alone is not a defect: the precedent html-css-js/fetch-and-browser-client lab covers five topics, and only three of them record 'module:'. The S32-only sentence came from the timing round at 95387e98 (sme-tm-1/edu-tm-1). That round matched the note to module.json, not to the six-topic, 8-task scope the lab already had. Not fixable as a scope cut in this lane, for three reasons. The lane must not weaken objective coverage. Fact 4 keeps the 8 tests and their names. Project 2 code is deferred: react/coding-lab/ does not exist and react course.json courseLabs is empty, so P3-P5 have no coded artifact yet, and cutting tasks 4-6 and 8 would leave CRUD, submission-error and UI-test objectives with no coded practice. Dependency check (reproduced): on the shipped starter, tests 4-7 all fail on the task 2 label message, and test 7 also needs tasks 4 (save) and 6 (delete toast). The only clean seam is tasks 1-3 | tasks 4-8. DECISION NEEDED (captain): where Standard learners do tasks 4-8. RECOMMENDED option A: keep the scope, tests, test names and minutes values. Sequence tasks 1-3 in the S32 guided-lab slot and tasks 4-8 in the S33 Build block, after S33's teach-then-check steps, as interim coded practice for P3-P5 until the deferred course project ships. Implement it as text only: (1) lab.json cleanup.notes: replace the S32-slot sentence with this two-slot sequencing and say the 25/30 planning allowance covers the whole task set. This supersedes the 95387e98 S32-only wording. (2) README: add a short 'When to do the tasks' note before 'The tasks'. (3) module.json sourceCoverageNotes: say the module lab covers all six topics, with tasks 4-8 run on S33 after the teach-then-check steps until the course project exists. Leave topic.json unchanged, per precedent. Option A is reversible and non-destructive. It edits only module-branch files and leaves the minutes values and every test unchanged. It does touch three earlier decisions, so whether it is in-scope is the captain's call: (i) it rewrites the allowance sentence that the course-owner directive 95387e98 scoped to the S32 slot; (ii) it brings back the two-slot phrasing that the accepted timing findings edu-tm-1/sme-tm-1 removed; (iii) it uses S33 Build time that intake budgets at 77 of 80 minutes for course-project parts P3-P5 (captain decision pep-project-rows), which are unbuilt while Project 2 is deferred. If the captain treats it as a sequencing decision for this lab program, it fits the auto-approval of recommended reversible corrections. Fallback B, not recommended: keep the whole lab in S32 and add a README pre-reading pointer to the three S33 topic pages. That practises before teaching. This is the only escalated high finding and it holds the critic gate until the decision lands.

Verified as reasoned, not measured: 8 tasks across 5 files, against the accepted fetch-and-browser-client lab at 38/45. The plausibility concern is fair and not reproducibly false. But estimatedMedian 25 / cap 30 is a course-owner directive (95387e98): planning allowances inside the frozen 120-minute/day calendar, not hard timers. Changing 'minutes' is outside this lab-correction lane. lab.json notes already say neither number is a measured learner pilot. DECISION NEEDED (course owner): whether to re-time the forms lab. RECOMMENDED: no change to 'minutes' now. Keep the existing not-a-pilot disclosure. The in-lane friction fixes (edu-fcc-4/-5/-6/-7/-9, sme-fcc-3/-4) reduce wasted time whatever edu-fcc-1 decides. Re-time from a learner pilot. If the captain adopts edu-fcc-1 option A, the work also spreads over two slots. Medium severity, so it does not block the critic gate.

Verified in starter/src/service-form.test.jsx lines 14-16. Step 5 tells learners to assert disappearance 'with findBy', which rejects when an element is absent, and contradicts its own parenthetical. It also says to 'type' a team although the control is a <select>. Fix (same file, comment only): rewrite step 5 as: type a name with user.type, choose a team with user.selectOptions, submit again, then assert with queryBy...not.toBeInTheDocument() that the error is gone and that onSave was called with the values (wrap in waitFor if needed). Apply together with sme-fcc-3.

Reproduced by the reconciler in a scratch copy of the reviewed snapshot (commit 402c4853) with the private reference overlay. A handleSubmit that sets fieldErrors only when validation fails (private mutant f2-noclear) passes all 7 public tests. Only the overlay's own learner test catches it, because the valid second submit navigates away and unmounts the form. Fix inside the existing test 3 (tests/t3-client-validation.test.jsx): set api.holdNextMutation = true before the second Save click. Then assert that both error texts are absent and neither field has aria-invalid='true', then call api.releaseHeld() and await the resulting navigation (for example findByRole on the new overview card) so no request is left in flight when the test ends. Do not use the 'fix only the name' alternative: f2 still overwrites errors whenever validation fails, so it would survive that check. Verified: f2 then fails test 3; the reference passes 8/8; the starter still fails all 8.

Verified: same step 5 defect as edu-fcc-4. Step 3's 'it renders after a state update, so pick the right query variant' implies getBy cannot work after an awaited user-event click, which over-states the topic's rule (the topic page teaches findBy for elements that appear later). Fix in the starter/src/service-form.test.jsx comment, together with edu-fcc-4: rewrite step 5 to use queryBy (or waitFor / waitForElementToBeRemoved) for absence. Reword step 3 to say findBy is the safe choice when an element may appear asynchronously, without implying getBy fails.
